author: Nayan Seth
description:
The personal rapport between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping is being put to its sternest test yet amid growing congressional pressure over AI chip curbs and broader calls in Washington for a more assertive policy on China, according to experts.
The two leaders are set to hold formal talks on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen.
While Trump may want to preserve a cordial rapport with Xi and a tactical thaw between...
title: Xi-Trump ties tested as calls grow in Washington for tougher China policy

author: Han Li,Lucy Quaggin
description:
Jurors began deliberating on Wednesday in the US government’s criminal case against Huawei Technologies, following a two-month trial that has been one of the most high-profile prosecutions of a Chinese technology giant in recent years.
Huawei, a Shenzhen-based company, is the world’s largest telecoms equipment maker and a major smartphone manufacturer. It faces 12 criminal counts, including racketeering conspiracy, stealing trade secrets, bank fraud and obstruction of justice.
US prosecutors...
title: Huawei case enters jury deliberations after 2-month battle in US courtroom

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi met Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday, marking a rare high-level contact at a time of deeply strained relations over Moscow’s war in Ukraine and the recent arrest of a Japanese journalist on espionage allegations.
The talks, held on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders’ summit in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, lasted about 30 minutes.
It was the first face-to-face encounter between the leaders of the two...
title: Japan’s Takaichi meets Putin in rare talks amid strained ties with Russia

author: Josephine Ma
description:
It was a day of firsts in Shenzhen on Wednesday when Chinese President Xi Jinping personally greeted his American counterpart Donald Trump at the city airport, setting up a historic start to the Apec summit.
It was the first time in nearly seven decades that China’s top leader had welcomed a visiting foreign head of state at an airport, and it set the stage for an international event that is likely to lead to a joint declaration by the 21 Apec members on Thursday.
Earlier in the day, Xi hosted...
title: Rare hug and roaring flyover set stage for historic firsts at Apec in Shenzhen

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
Handshakes, warm welcomes and carefully staged photo opportunities defined US President Donald Trump’s first day in Shenzhen on Wednesday, as China showcased its diplomatic priorities ahead of a planned three-way summit with Russia.
Here are the key moments from the day.
Xi’s personal welcome for Trump
Chinese President Xi Jinping broke with decades of protocol by personally greeting Trump at Shenzhen Baon Airport.
Their handshake quickly turned into a brief hug, while five J-10C fighter jets...
title: A tarmac hug with Xi and a handshake with Putin, how Trump began his China visit

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Chinese replenishment ships were seen repeatedly transiting two major waterways around Japan as the Liaoning aircraft carrier conducted an extended western Pacific Ocean deployment that could test its 40-day endurance record.
According to Japanese defence ministry statements, the ships made at least eight crossings through the Miyako Strait and the Osumi Strait between October 16 and Wednesday, the South China Morning Post calculated.
The straits are strategically important in southwestern Japan...
title: How China’s ‘carrier nannies’ are powering the Liaoning’s long Pacific push

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan again let her English do the talking as she accompanied President Xi Jinping in welcoming his US counterpart Donald Trump and other leaders to Shenzhen for the Apec summit’s welcome dinner.
On Wednesday night, leaders gathered at the Shenzhen International Communication Centre for a welcome banquet and cultural gala ahead of Thursday’s main meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation event.
Peng arrived in her classic understated style: a light pink dress with...
title: China’s first lady Peng Liyuan again lets her English do the talking in welcoming Trump

author: Fan Chen
description:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Chinese President Xi Jinping had their first in-person interaction in Shenzhen since last autumn, when ties froze due to her controversial remarks on Taiwan.
Takaichi shook hands with Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, as they posed for greeting photos ahead of the customary Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) “family photo” on Wednesday evening, according to a live feed of a welcome dinner for the Apec gathering.
Takaichi, dressed in a fluorescent pink...
title: Xi greets Takaichi with a smile – but no words – as China-Japan freeze lingers

author: Alyssa Chen,Amber Wang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and first lady Peng Liyuan welcomed Apec leaders to a gala dinner in Shenzhen on Wednesday night where every dish and musical performance was chosen to tell a story.
Earlier in the evening, the heads of government gathered at the lakeside Shenzhen International Communication Centre for the traditional family photo before heading to a banquet that put Guangdong’s famed cuisine centre stage – alongside a few international touches for the visitors.
Rather than relying...
title: Classic Cantonese dim sum and music from around the world on the menu for Apec banquet

author: Fan Chen
description:
US President Donald Trump received a historic red-carpet welcome from Chinese President Xi Jinping upon arriving in Shenzhen on Wednesday as the leaders prepare for high-stakes talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit.
Xi personally greeted Trump on the tarmac on Wednesday afternoon, reciprocating the rare welcome the Chinese leader received upon arriving in Washington for a state visit in September.
Wednesday’s welcome marked the first time in nearly seven decades that...
title: Returning the favour, Xi personally welcomes Trump ahead of high-stakes Apec talks

author: Eve Qiao
description:
The Apec summit in Shenzhen is something of a homecoming for Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul.
Anutin can trace his family roots back to southern China, and when he was asked on Wednesday how it felt to be in Guangdong province, he burst out laughing and replied in Cantonese.
“Hou hoi sam!” he said, which means “so happy”.
In a video published by state news agency China News Service, Anutin likened China and Thailand to siblings, saying their ties went beyond an ordinary partnership.
“I...
title: For the Thai prime minister, Apec in Shenzhen is almost home ground

author: Hao Nan
description:
Gulf governments are building collective defences while exploring security arrangements with the very country many of those defences are designed to deter.
On November 5, Turkey’s parliament approved a mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. Five days later, the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) agreed to establish a military command in Kuwait. In between, Iran’s foreign minister contacted 12 regional counterparts, calling for security arrangements without outside powers.
These are...
title: The big test facing the Middle East’s emerging security autonomy

author: Victoria Bela
description:
For years, engineers around the world have experimented with mounting guns on drones to boost battlefield firepower.
But a new study by Chinese researchers shows that unmanned vehicles could be used to shoot a very different kind of ammunition – rice.
In a paper published last month, the researchers detailed an optimised pump system that could use precise, high-pressure jets to plant rice rather than randomly scattering the seeds.
“This study proposes a seed-metering pump designed for a...
title: Field of fire: Chinese scientists develop drone gun that can plant rice more efficiently

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit amid strained ties between Beijing and Tokyo.
The low-key arrival marking the first China visit by a Japanese leader in seven years contrasted sharply with the warm welcome given to South Korean President Lee Jae Myung earlier in the day.
On the tarmac, Takaichi was met by retired Chinese diplomat Zhang Qiyue and Japanese ambassador to China Kenji Kanasugi before she nodded...
title: Takaichi makes low-key arrival in Shenzhen after Lee is greeted by dancers

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
A bipartisan US commission urged Congress on Wednesday to require companies exporting advanced artificial intelligence chips to China to certify that the shipments would not divert manufacturing capacity from the US market, adding a new proposal to the debate over chip controls ahead of President Donald Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, a bipartisan panel created by Congress to assess the national security implications of...
title: US panel proposes tougher AI chip export rules ahead of Xi-Trump talks

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
The butterflies that enchanted the South Korean and Chinese leaders at last year’s Apec summit in Gyeongju have been revived in Shenzhen as a symbol of the growing momentum in bilateral ties.
Butterflies were the emblem of the Gyeongju summit, and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday suggested they had made the journey to China.
Lee made the remarks in a social media post soon after he arrived in Shenzhen and held his third bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping since...
title: Will Xi get his wish for the butterflies, and bilateral ties, to ‘fly even better’?

author: Dewey Sim
description:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Wednesday that ties with China were “growing on every front” after the two countries agreed to ease trade restrictions, but brushed off suggestions that it was a threat to the United States.
Carney also said he had raised the global governance of artificial intelligence when he met Chinese President Xi Jinping the previous day, setting out Canada’s “model for how this governance can be developed”.
Relations between the two countries have been improving...
title: Carney hails ‘real progress’ in China-Canada ties but suggests US has no need to worry

author: Phoebe Zhang,Josephine Ma,Amber Wang
description:
While the key Apec meetings this week will be held at the Shenzhen International Exchange Centre, much of the diplomatic manoeuvring will take place at a secluded government-owned lakeside resort in the southern Chinese city’s northwest.
Kylin Villa, a five-star garden resort nestled in the rolling foothills of Qilin Mountain, has been chosen as the venue for high-profile meetings on the sidelines, including the talks between Chinese President Xi Jinping and his US and Russian counterparts...
title: Kylin Villa – China’s 5-star lakeside resort with a presidential mission for Apec

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping called for deeper cooperation on trade and technology in the Asia-Pacific region and hit out at protectionism, a day after the United States moved to further curb China’s access to high-end computer chips.
“China has stood up to unilateralism and protectionism and remained committed to true multilateralism,” Xi said at the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen. “No matter how the international landscape changes, China will not waver in its pursuit of win-win cooperation with...
title: Xi touts China AI amid Shenzhen’s tech showcase

author: SCMP Reporters
description:
This live article is freely available to our registered users. Please log in or create an account.
US President Donald Trump has landed in Shenzhen for the Apec Summit.
It marks Trump’s second trip to China this year, after his May state visit to Beijing, where the leaders of the two countries agreed to build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability.
The US president’s visit follows a decisive midterm election defeat for his Republican Party barely two weeks ago. It also...
title: Xi Jinping personally greets Trump as he arrives in Shenzhen for Apec, 3-way talks

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for a joint effort to safeguard global supply chains, deepen economic policy coordination and foster cooperation on artificial intelligence and other emerging tech industries in a meeting with his South Korean counterpart Lee Jae Myung in Shenzhen on Wednesday.
During the 34-minute meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen, Xi hailed the “substantial conclusion” of the second phase of the two...
title: Xi Jinping urges South Korea to cooperate with China on AI and supply chains

author: Robin Hu
description:
Every Chinese New Year, a finance official in an eastern Chinese county braces for visitors. They run businesses to which his county owes money. When the county lacks the money to pay, he sometimes stops answering his phone. He described those visits to The Economic Observer, a business weekly.
Beijing has now taken his problem and made it his superiors’ problem. In a report to China’s legislature published on November 5, the State Council said the number of local government financing vehicles –...
title: China’s local officials feel financial stick long before seeing carrot

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
The fist came before the flags. As US President Donald Trump stepped off Air Force One in Manila on Tuesday evening, he raised a clenched fist towards the cameras, accepted miniature American and Philippine flags from a child and waved them down the red carpet.
Roughly 20 hours later, as he departed Manila for Shenzhen in southern China, Trump again raised his fist towards the cameras.
Experts said the sequence which opened his first foreign trip since Republicans lost both chambers of Congress...
title: Flags, fists and an extra 5 minutes: Manila reveals a confident but tired Trump

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage on science from the past two weeks to help you stay informed. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. 40 Chinese spaceplanes could hit any target on Earth in minutes: study
A newly released photograph in a US intelligence report has offered a rare glimpse of what is widely believed to be China’s secret Shenlong spaceplane in orbit, showing its payload bay doors open.
2. ‘10,000-tonne level talent’ biologist...
title: Chinese spaceplanes’ global reach, a study on erectile dysfunction: 7 science highlights

author: Eve Qiao
description:
When Russia’s President Vladimir Putin stepped off his plane in Shenzhen early on Wednesday for the Apec summit and the unprecedented trilateral talks with his Chinese and US counterparts, his trusty limousine was waiting for him on the runway.
Greeted by Cai Qi, a member of the Communist Party’s Politburo Standing Committee, Putin waved to the crowd and climbed into his black Aurus Senat limousine, which had a small Russian flag mounted at its nose.
The Russian-built presidential limousine has...
title: Putin brings a signature diplomatic tool with him to Shenzhen – his limousine

author: Carol Yang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin pledged to maintain stable bilateral ties and advance a multipolar world amid mounting global uncertainties during their meeting on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday, ahead of their landmark trilateral summit with the United States.
Highlighting the resilience of bilateral relations, Xi said China-Russia ties “stand as firm as a mountain amid wind and rain” and called for taking a long-term strategic...
title: Xi and Putin say they will maintain stable ties, seek ‘more fair multipolar world order’

author: Han Li
description:
A US federal court in New York spent another long day on Tuesday hearing closing arguments from Chinese tech giant Huawei Technologies in the final stage of a high-profile trial that once inflamed tensions between Washington and Beijing.
The case has dragged on for nearly eight years, and the trial has been under way since September, with prosecutors commencing closing arguments on Monday.
Huawei and three affiliated companies face 12 criminal counts, including racketeering conspiracy, which US...
title: Huawei calls US prosecution’s case ‘fictionalised portrait’ in closing arguments

author: Orange Wang
description:
China has given Russian President Vladimir Putin the highest-level welcome so far among foreign leaders arriving in Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gathering.
Putin’s Ilyushin Il-96 aircraft touched down at Baoan International Airport in the southern Chinese city shortly after 2am on Wednesday, marking his second trip to China this year and his 26th since taking office.
Live-stream footage and state media reports showed Cai Qi – chief of staff to President Xi Jinping and...
title: Putin gets highest-level airport welcome in Shenzhen as he arrives for Apec

author: Liu Zhen
description:
The Beast – as the state car serving the United States leader is popularly known – is expected to make its second trip to China in half a year when President Donald Trump arrives in Shenzhen on Wednesday for the Apec leaders’ summit.
This time, however, the heavily armoured presidential limousine, officially named Cadillac One, will find itself sharing the roads with a very different kind of motorcade.

The Beast is widely reported to be powered by a V8 engine, with some reports putting its fuel...
title: Heavy metal in an EV hub: Trump’s ‘Beast’ and new Air Force One to touch down in Shenzhen

author: Shi Huang
description:
For the more than 1.5 billion people worldwide who suffer from androgenetic alopecia, combing their hair before the mirror each morning is a routine that is often accompanied by quiet anxiety.
However, this most ordinary everyday tool may hold the key to reversing hair loss, according to a Chinese research team which developed a comb that uses microelectronics to treat hair loss.
A study on mice has found that nearly 100 per cent hair coverage was achieved in just 28 days using the device,...
title: Chinese scientists’ magic comb restores hair growth by nearly 100% in mice study

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast told Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday that he represented “the state, not a political faction”, in their first meeting since he took office in March, after disputes over a Chinese undersea cable and a UN treaty body strained ties with Chile’s largest trading partner.
The two leaders met in Shenzhen a day before the southern Chinese city hosts the Apec leaders’ summit, in a year that marks a decade of their comprehensive strategic partnership and two...
title: Chile’s Kast meets China’s Xi for first time to steady ties strained by US pressure
